The '''China-United States Exchange Foundation''' ('''CUSEF''') is a Hong Kong-based [[nonprofit organization]] whose stated aim is to encourage dialogue and exchanges between the people of the United States and China. CUSEF was founded in 2008 by [[Tung Chee-hwa]], a billionaire, former [[Chief Executive of Hong Kong]], and former [[Vice Chairperson of the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference|vice chairperson]] of the [[Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference]] (CPPCC), who remained the chairman emeritus of the foundation until his death in 2026.<ref name=":1">{{Cite news|last=Allen-Ebrahimian|first=Bethany|date=November 28, 2017|title=This Beijing-Linked Billionaire Is Funding Policy Research at Washington's Most Influential Institutions: The Chinese Communist Party is quietly reshaping public opinion and policy abroad.|work=[[Foreign Policy]]|url=https://foreignpolicy.com/2017/11/28/this-beijing-linked-billionaire-is-funding-policy-research-at-washingtons-most-influential-institutions-china-dc/|access-date=September 20, 2020|archive-date=August 31, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190831001044/https://foreignpolicy.com/2017/11/28/this-beijing-linked-billionaire-is-funding-policy-research-at-washingtons-most-influential-institutions-china-dc/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |title=Tung Chee-hwa elected Chairman Emeritus of China-United States Exchange Foundation |url=https://www.thestandard.com.hk/breaking-news/section/4/209729/Tung-Chee-hwa-elected-Chairman-Emeritus-of-China-United-States-Exchange-Foundation |access-date=2024-10-28 |website=The Standard |language=en}}</ref> CUSEF's governing board has included members such as [[Ronnie Chan]], [[Elsie Leung]], and [[Victor Fung (businessman)|Victor Fung]].<ref name=":2" /> Foundation donors include multiple CPPCC members.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Yu |first=Cheryl |date=March 28, 2025 |title=The Party's One-Way Approach to People-to-People Exchanges |url=https://jamestown.org/program/the-partys-one-way-approach-to-people-to-people-exchanges/ |access-date=2025-03-28 |website=[[Jamestown Foundation]] |language=en-US |archive-date=22 December 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251222213231/http://jamestown.org/program/the-partys-one-way-approach-to-people-to-people-exchanges/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

CUSEF is supervised by the [[Chinese People's Association for Friendship with Foreign Countries]].<ref name=":4" /> CUSEF donates to universities and think tanks in the U.S. while also sponsoring trips for journalists, students, and former U.S. officials and politicians to China to speak with officials.<ref>{{Cite news|last=Allen-Ebrahimian|first=Bethany|date=June 30, 2020|title=China's influence operations are getting harder to hide|work=[[Axios (website)|Axios]]|url=https://www.axios.com/chinas-influence-operations-are-getting-harder-to-hide-462c6ed5-bfd5-4ba0-a92d-fd3c1593d444.html|access-date=September 20, 2020|archive-date=September 23, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200923072923/https://www.axios.com/chinas-influence-operations-are-getting-harder-to-hide-462c6ed5-bfd5-4ba0-a92d-fd3c1593d444.html|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name=":3" /> According to various journalists and academics, CUSEF is a central part of the [[Chinese Communist Party]]'s [[United Front (China)|united front]] strategy of influence in the U.S.<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite book|last1=Cole|first1=J. Michael|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=WTO-zQEACAAJ|title=Insidious Power: How China Undermines Global Democracy|last2=Hsu|first2=Szu-Chien|date=2020-07-30|publisher=Eastbridge Books|isbn=978-1-78869-214-4|pages=29–37, 56–57|language=en|access-date=2020-09-20|archive-date=2021-06-06|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210606181944/https://books.google.com/books?id=WTO-zQEACAAJ|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|last1=Hamilton|first1=Clive|title=Hidden Hand: Exposing How the Chinese Communist Party Is Reshaping the World|last2=Ohlberg|first2=Mareike|date=2020|publisher=Oneworld Publications|isbn=978-1-78607-784-4|location=New York|pages=210–212|language=en|oclc=1150166864|author-link=Clive Hamilton}}</ref><ref name="USCC2018">{{cite web |last=Bowe |first=Alexander |date=August 24, 2018 |title=China's Overseas United Front Work: Background and Implications for the United States |url=https://www.uscc.gov/sites/default/files/Research/China%27s%20Overseas%20United%20Front%20Work%20-%20Background%20and%20Implications%20for%20US_final_0.pdf |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180909101348/https://www.uscc.gov/sites/default/files/Research/China%27s%20Overseas%20United%20Front%20Work%20-%20Background%20and%20Implications%20for%20US_final_0.pdf |archive-date=9 September 2018 |access-date=May 12, 2019 |publisher=[[United States-China Economic and Security Review Commission]] }}</ref>

== History ==
According to [[Foreign Agents Registration Act]] (FARA) filings, CUSEF is classified as a "foreign principal" which has hired lobbying and public relations firms since 2009 such as [[Brown Lloyd James]], Fontheim International, [[Covington & Burling]], Capitol Counsel LLC, [[Podesta Group]], and [[Wilson Global Communications]] to craft and promote pro-Beijing messages.<ref>{{Cite news|last=Dotson|first=John|date=September 16, 2020|title=The China-U.S. Exchange Foundation and United Front "Lobbying Laundering" in American Politics|url=https://jamestown.org/program/the-china-u-s-exchange-foundation-and-united-front-lobbying-laundering-in-american-politics/|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200920160222/https://jamestown.org/program/the-china-u-s-exchange-foundation-and-united-front-lobbying-laundering-in-american-politics/|archive-date=September 20, 2020|access-date=September 19, 2020|website=[[Jamestown Foundation]]}}</ref><ref name=":3">{{Cite news|last1=Lim|first1=Louisa|last2=Bergin|first2=Julia|date=2018-12-07|title=Inside China's audacious global propaganda campaign|language=en-GB|work=[[The Guardian]]|url=https://www.theguardian.com/news/2018/dec/07/china-plan-for-global-media-dominance-propaganda-xi-jinping|url-status=live|access-date=2019-08-31|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200310193251/https://www.theguardian.com/news/2018/dec/07/china-plan-for-global-media-dominance-propaganda-xi-jinping|archive-date=2020-03-10|issn=0261-3077}}</ref>

In 2023, CUSEF launched a campaign to lobby members of the [[Congressional Black Caucus]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=30 August 2023 |title=Lobby firm woos African Americans to promote China's foreign influence ops |url=https://www.intelligenceonline.com/corporate-intelligence/2023/08/30/lobby-firm-woos-african-americans-to-promote-china-s-foreign-influence-ops,110037374-eve |url-access=subscription |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230920123829/https://www.intelligenceonline.com/corporate-intelligence/2023/08/30/lobby-firm-woos-african-americans-to-promote-china-s-foreign-influence-ops,110037374-eve |archive-date=20 September 2023 |access-date=4 December 2023 |work=[[Intelligence Online]]}}</ref>

=== Sanya Initiative ===
Since 2008, CUSEF has partnered with the [[China Association for International Friendly Contact]] and the [[EastWest Institute]] to organize forums, termed the U.S.-China Sanya Initiative, between retired [[People's Liberation Army]] (PLA) officers and retired U.S. military personnel.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Sanya Initiative|url=https://www.cusef.org.hk/en/what-we-do/high-level-dialogues/sanya-initiative|access-date=2020-09-20|website=China-United States Exchange Foundation|language=en|archive-date=2020-10-23|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201023061443/https://www.cusef.org.hk/en/what-we-do/high-level-dialogues/sanya-initiative|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=Cavanaugh|first=Joshua|date=June 3, 2020|title=U.S.-China Sanya Initiative Dialogue: Report from the 11th Meeting|url=https://www.eastwest.ngo/idea/us-china-sanya-initiative-dialogue-report-11th-meeting|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200905224025/https://www.eastwest.ngo/idea/us-china-sanya-initiative-dialogue-report-11th-meeting|archive-date=2020-09-05|access-date=2020-09-05|website=[[EastWest Institute]]}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite journal |last=Wortzel |first=Larry M. |author-link=Larry Wortzel |date=March 1, 2014 |title=The Chinese People's Liberation Army and Information Warfare |journal=Monographs, Collaborative Studies, & Irps |url=https://press.armywarcollege.edu/monographs/506/ |publisher=[[Strategic Studies Institute]] |pages=33–34 |jstor=resrep11757 |jstor-access=free |access-date=December 4, 2023 |archive-date=October 30, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221030155241/https://press.armywarcollege.edu/monographs/506/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Past forums were reported to have attempted to influence retired U.S. military officers to lobby against [[List of US arms sales to Taiwan|U.S. arms sales to Taiwan]] and to delay a Pentagon report on PLA capabilities.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Kan|first=Shirley A.|date=July 25, 2013|title=U.S.-China Military Contacts: Issues for Congress|url=https://apps.dtic.mil/sti/pdfs/ADA585310.pdf|url-status=live|language=en|publisher=[[Congressional Research Service]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200927040954/https://apps.dtic.mil/sti/pdfs/ADA585310.pdf|archive-date=September 27, 2020|access-date=September 27, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Garnaut |first=John |date=2013-05-24 |title=China gets into the business of making friends |url=https://www.smh.com.au/world/china-gets-into-the-business-of-making-friends-20130524-2k6q3.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200706000048/https://www.smh.com.au/world/china-gets-into-the-business-of-making-friends-20130524-2k6q3.html |archive-date=2020-07-06 |access-date=2020-07-06 |website=[[The Sydney Morning Herald]] |language=en}}</ref>

=== Trips for elected officials ===
In 2019, CUSEF sponsored a trip to China by a delegation of mayors from Indiana, Ohio, and South Dakota, including [[James Brainard]] and [[Paul TenHaken]].<ref>{{Cite web |last= |date=2019-11-30 |title=Fall 2019 Mayors Delegation to China |url=https://usheartlandchina.org/delegations/fall-2019-mayors-delegation-to-china/ |access-date=2023-09-28 |website=United States Heartland China Association |language=en-US |archive-date=2023-05-30 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230530220347/https://usheartlandchina.org/delegations/fall-2019-mayors-delegation-to-china/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

=== University funding and other activities ===
CUSEF has funded the Pacific Community Initiative at the [[Paul H. Nitze School of Advanced International Studies]] at [[Johns Hopkins University]].<ref name=":02">{{Cite book |last1=Diamond |first1=Larry |author-link=Larry Diamond |url=https://www.hoover.org/research/chinas-influence-american-interests-promoting-constructive-vigilance |title=China's Influence and American Interests: Promoting Constructive Vigilance |last2=Schell |first2=Orville |author-link2=Orville Schell |date=2019-08-01 |publisher=[[Hoover Institution]] |isbn=978-0-8179-2286-3 |pages=61 |language=en |oclc=1104533323 |access-date=September 4, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200528122006/https://www.hoover.org/research/chinas-influence-american-interests-promoting-constructive-vigilance |archive-date=2020-05-28 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Pacific Community Initiative |url=https://sais.jhu.edu/pacific-community-initiative |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201021012054/https://sais.jhu.edu/pacific-community-initiative |archive-date=2020-10-21 |access-date=2020-10-18 |website=[[Paul H. Nitze School of Advanced International Studies]]|date=29 January 2020 }}</ref> CUSEF also provides funding to the [[University of Montana]]'s Max S. Baucus Institute.<ref name="nr-defies" />

In 2018, the [[University of Texas at Austin]] refused a donation from CUSEF after a letter by Senator [[Ted Cruz]] raised concerns about the foundation's reported links to the Chinese Communist Party.<ref name=":2">{{Cite news|last1=Lam|first1=Jeffie|last2=Chung|first2=Kimmy|date=January 15, 2018|title=University of Texas at Austin rejects funding from Hong Kong-based foundation, citing its links to Communist Party|work=[[South China Morning Post]]|url=https://www.scmp.com/news/hong-kong/education/article/2128338/university-texas-austin-rejects-funding-hong-kong-based|access-date=September 20, 2020|archive-date=November 9, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201109024801/http://www.scmp.com/news/hong-kong/education/article/2128338/university-texas-austin-rejects-funding-hong-kong-based|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|last=Redden|first=Elizabeth|date=January 16, 2018|title=Thanks, but No, Thanks|work=[[Inside Higher Ed]]|url=https://www.insidehighered.com/news/2018/01/16/ut-austin-rejects-funding-chinese-government-linked-foundation|access-date=September 20, 2020|archive-date=September 20, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200920160234/https://www.insidehighered.com/news/2018/01/16/ut-austin-rejects-funding-chinese-government-linked-foundation|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|last=Rogin|first=Josh|date=January 15, 2018|title=University rejects Chinese Communist Party-linked influence efforts on campus|language=en-US|newspaper=[[The Washington Post]]|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/opinions/global-opinions/university-rejects-chinese-communist-party-linked-influence-efforts-on-campus/2018/01/14/c454b54e-f7de-11e7-beb6-c8d48830c54d_story.html|access-date=2020-09-20|issn=0190-8286|archive-date=2020-12-15|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201215013837/https://www.washingtonpost.com/opinions/global-opinions/university-rejects-chinese-communist-party-linked-influence-efforts-on-campus/2018/01/14/c454b54e-f7de-11e7-beb6-c8d48830c54d_story.html|url-status=live|author-link=Josh Rogin}}</ref> In 2023, US House representatives [[Mike Gallagher (American politician)|Mike Gallagher]], [[Ryan Zinke]], and [[Matt Rosendale]] pressed the University of Montana to cut ties with CUSEF related to its funding of student trips to China.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Quinn |first=Jimmy |date=4 December 2023 |title=Obama China Ambassador's Institute Faces Scrutiny over Beijing Ties |work=[[National Review]] |url=https://www.nationalreview.com/2023/12/obama-china-ambassadors-institute-faces-scrutiny-over-beijing-ties/ |access-date=4 December 2023 |archive-date=4 December 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231204183450/https://www.nationalreview.com/2023/12/obama-china-ambassadors-institute-faces-scrutiny-over-beijing-ties/ |url-status=live }}</ref> The university declined to end the program. Its president, [[Seth Bodnar]], said the program was "in complete compliance with state and federal law" and that the university's responsibility was to "expand learning experiences for our students so that America can compete and win around the globe."<ref name="dil-zinke">{{cite news |last=Heston |first=Kate |title=Zinke calls on University of Montana to drop exchange program with China |work=Daily Inter Lake |date=December 7, 2023 |url=https://dailyinterlake.com/news/2023/dec/07/zinke-rejects-um-partnership-with-china/ |access-date=August 24, 2026}}</ref><ref name="nr-defies">{{Cite news |last=Quinn |first=Jimmy |title=University of Montana Defies Call to Shutter Program Linked to Chinese Influence Operation |work=[[National Review]] |date=January 2, 2024 |url=https://www.nationalreview.com/corner/university-of-montana-defies-call-to-shutter-program-linked-to-chinese-influence-operation/ |access-date=August 24, 2026}}</ref> A university spokesman said CUSEF was not listed on the federal Consolidated Screening List and that the university complied with a Montana law requiring disclosure of partnerships with foreign countries of concern.<ref name="nr-defies" /> In January 2026, CUSEF organized a trip to China for a group of [[Harvard University]] students where they met with [[Lu Kang (diplomat)|Lu Kang]] of the [[International Department of the Chinese Communist Party]].<ref name=":4">{{Cite web |last=Reisboard |first=Jonah |date=February 17, 2026 |title=Recent ILD Activity Suggests Expanded Mandate |url=https://jamestown.org/recent-ild-activity-suggests-expanded-mandate/ |access-date=2026-02-23 |website=[[Jamestown Foundation]]}}</ref>

=== Foundation grants ===
In 2021, CUSEF gave a $5 million grant to the George H.W. Bush Foundation for U.S.-China Relations.<ref>{{Cite news|last1=Lachlan|first1=Markay|last2=Allen-Ebrahimian|first2=Bethany|date=June 5, 2021|title=Bush family nonprofit's $5 million deal with China influence group|work=[[Axios (website)|Axios]]|url=https://www.axios.com/scoop-bush-family-nonprofits-5-million-deal-with-china-influence-group-886e7d7a-36c3-471b-a582-31b0c2e50eeb.html|access-date=June 6, 2021|archive-date=June 6, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210606032825/https://www.axios.com/scoop-bush-family-nonprofits-5-million-deal-with-china-influence-group-886e7d7a-36c3-471b-a582-31b0c2e50eeb.html|url-status=live}}</ref> CUSEF also provides funding to the [[Carter Center]]<ref>{{Cite news|last1=Eisenman|first1=Joshua|last2=Sobolik|first2=Michael|date=August 31, 2021|title=U.S. Institutions Must Get Smarter About Chinese Communist Party Money|url=https://foreignpolicy.com/2021/08/31/chinese-communist-party-money-us-institutions/|url-status=live|access-date=2021-09-05|website=[[Foreign Policy]]|language=en-US|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210831212848/https://foreignpolicy.com/2021/08/31/chinese-communist-party-money-us-institutions/ |archive-date=2021-08-31 }}</ref> and has partnered with the [[Carnegie Endowment for International Peace]], [[Brookings Institution]], [[Atlantic Council]], and [[Center for American Progress]].<ref name="USCC2018" />

=== Hong Kong Forum on US-China Relations ===
CUSEF periodically holds the "Hong Kong Forum on US-China Relations" to facilitate exchanges between present and former officials, academics, and business leaders in the US, China, and other nations. In 2023, speakers attending the forum include former US ambassador to China and ex-senator [[Max Baucus]], former US Trade Negotiator [[Charlene Barshefsky]] and President of the 70th Session of the UN General Assembly [[Mogens Lykketoft]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-10-08 |title=US, UN officials to attend Hong Kong forum on Sino-US ties in November |url=https://www.scmp.com/news/hong-kong/politics/article/3237226/us-un-officials-attend-hong-kong-forum-sino-us-ties-november-hosted-tung-chee-hwas-foundation |access-date=2024-10-28 |website=[[South China Morning Post]] |language=en |archive-date=16 July 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250716002646/https://www.scmp.com/news/hong-kong/politics/article/3237226/us-un-officials-attend-hong-kong-forum-sino-us-ties-november-hosted-tung-chee-hwas-foundation |url-status=live }}</ref>

==== Hong Kong Forum 2024 ====
The forum in 2024 included speeches from [[Xie Feng (diplomat)|Xie Feng]], China's ambassador to the United States, and Nicholas Burns, the US ambassador to China delivered through video. The forum was attended by former ambassador [[Max Baucus]], the 12th United States Trade Representative [[Charlene Barshefsky]], representatives from families of former US president Carter, Nixon, and Bush.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hu |first=Oasis |title=Forum on US-China ties set to launch |url=https://www.chinadailyhk.com/hk/article/597241 |access-date=2024-11-17 |website=[[China Daily]] |archive-date=10 November 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251110223026/https://www.chinadailyhk.com/hk/article/597241 |url-status=live }}</ref>

[[John Moolenaar]], chairman of the [[United States House Select Committee on Strategic Competition between the United States and the Chinese Communist Party]], and [[Fox News]] has criticized US officials from attending the forum, stating that it would "legitimize the CCP event."<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-11-15 |title=Moolenaar: U.S. Participation in CUSEF Forum Sends the Wrong Message |url=https://selectcommitteeontheccp.house.gov/media/press-releases/moolenaar-us-participation-cusef-forum-sends-wrong-message |access-date=2024-11-17 |website=[[Select Committee on the CCP]] |language=en |archive-date=29 October 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251029010251/https://selectcommitteeontheccp.house.gov/media/press-releases/moolenaar-us-participation-cusef-forum-sends-wrong-message |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Andrew Miller |first=Cameron Cawthorne |date=2024-11-13 |title='Malign influence': Top Biden official faces backlash ahead of address at forum with deep ties to CCP |url=https://www.foxnews.com/politics/malign-influence-top-biden-official-faces-backlash-ahead-address-forum-deep-ties-ccp |access-date=2024-11-17 |website=[[Fox News]] |language=en-US |archive-date=29 April 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250429165437/https://www.foxnews.com/politics/malign-influence-top-biden-official-faces-backlash-ahead-address-forum-deep-ties-ccp |url-status=live }}</ref>
